gaps.sentence: 'We've been waiting for hours,' the passengers complained. The passengers complained that they ___ waiting for hours.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been waiting → had been waiting after the past reporting verb 'complained'.

gaps.sentence: 'Are you coming to the party?' they asked me. They asked ___ coming to the party.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions become if/whether clauses; pronouns and tenses shift: if I was coming.

gaps.sentence: 'Why did you cancel the order?' he asked. He asked why I ___ the order.
gaps.explanation: Wh-questions keep the wh-word but drop do-support and backshift: did you cancel → I had cancelled.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.

gaps.sentence: She ___ that she would be waiting by the main entrance.
gaps.hint: say takes no personal object here
gaps.explanation: Say (that)... without a personal object; 'told that' is impossible without the object.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you ever been to Iceland?' she asked. She asked ___ ever been to Iceland.
gaps.explanation: Have you been → if I had been: if/whether with past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'The earth goes round the sun,' the teacher said. The teacher said that the earth ___ round the sun.
gaps.explanation: Timeless general truths may keep the present simple after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll carry those bags for you,' he said. He ___ to carry my bags.
gaps.explanation: Offers of help are reported as offered to do something.
